steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Spray a 2-quart casserole dish with cooking spray.
Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rapid boil. Cook egg noodles at a boil until tender yet firm to the bite, 7 to 9 minutes. Drain and transfer to a large mixing bowl.
Add tuna, celery, and green onions to the noodles. Stir in mayonnaise, sour cream, mustard, thyme, and salt until well combined.

Spoon 1/2 of the noodle mixture into the prepared casserole dish, then layer 1/2 of the zucchini slices over top. Repeat layers once more, then sprinkle Monterey Jack cheese over the entire casserole.
Bake in the preheated oven until hot and bubbly, about 30 minutes.
Remove from the oven and sprinkle with chopped tomato before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Hearty Tuna Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This tuna noodle casserole with sour cream may not be your grandma’s, but it is sure to please everybody in the family.

review.reviewBody: I've made this several times now and it is a favourite! I brown the onion and celery first, substitute the sour cream with yogurt and add 1/2 tsp each of dill, basil and pepper. Sometimes I will substitute the zucchini with a package of thawed spinach. I usually just mix everything (instead of layering) together.

This was really wonderful! I adapted what I did based on what I had on hand, hubby's allergies, and reviews. Hubby is allergic to zucchini, so I used some green beans that were about to go bad, cut into 1 inch pieces. I sauted those with the onion and celery, at this point I also added 2 large cloves pressed garlic. I didn't have egg noodles, I used instead a large Italian corkscrew pasta with ridges. I had a 12 oz can of tuna, so I used the whole thing. And I swapped the sour cream and mayonnaise measurements. I didn't have tomato so instead added a small palm full of capers, drained. For cheese I used half sharp cheddar and half asiago. In addition to the salt I added lots of black pepper, 3 shakes cayanne pepper, and 3 Tbsp fine chopped fresh parsley. I mixed in half the cheese with the rest of the ingredients, and then sprinkled the other half on top. Then I sprinkled on 4 Tbsp Italian bread crumbs. Baked as instructed and browned under the broiler on high for the last 2 mins. Amazing! I left out the mustard and put in 1/3 cup of cream because people said it was dry and that they didn't like the mustard flavor. With all these changes it was amazing! Really happy to have a recipe that doesn't have cream of condensed whatever in the ingredients list. Thanks so much!

This is a fantastic, away from the normal, tuna casserole. I had to make some changes, because I did not have the cheese on hand that the recipe called for. The following is what I did. I doubled the recipe and with that instead of the shredded cheese, I used one 8 oz. package of cream cheese. I did not use the zucchini due to I have a son who does not like zucchini, instead I added 12oz. Package of frozen peas. ( remember, I doubled the recipe make sure to double the recipe ingredients, use amount I listed for subs) I made noodles as directed and I took every other ingredient and mixed it in a large sauce pan and blended all together until cream cheese was melted. I then poured the sauce over the already cooked noodles, and mixed/ blended all together. I put it in a large baking dish in a pre- heated oven at 350 degrees F and baked for approx. 30 minutes, just until warmed all the way through and the top began to brown. This fed a family of 5 with 4 of them being very hearty eaters. THEY LOVED IT. thank you for posting your recipe, I would not have been able to make the dish I did with out it.

I made a few small changes- no zucchini and I added Pablo and butter topping to give it some crunch. I sautéed the celery and onions before I tossed everything together. I used champagne dill mustard for a little extra zip. I will make this regularly!

delicious. made as written, with additions: added red bell peppper and another can of tuna and a little more "wet" ingredients (sour cream and mayonnaise) to mix up the add'l tuna. also added dill weed. Topped casserole with black pepper and paprika. After cooking for 25 minutes, added french fried onions and cooked for last 5 minutes. Very tasty.

The best tuna noodle casserole I've ever made. I was a little skeptical about the use of mayo, mustard and sour cream, but we really liked it and it was much easier than making a homemade cream sauce. I made it with whole grain noodles and a no-drain packet of albacore tuna, and cheddar instead of Jack cheese. I also tossed in some sliced fresh mushrooms with the zucchini. I forgot the tomato at the end, but we didn't miss it. I recommend preparing everything exactly as instructed--don't cook the onion and celery beforehand because they don't need it. The celery came out a little on the crunchy side, but that little bit of cruch is a nice contrast with the otherwise soft, creamy casserole. Definitely will make this again!

Surprisingly good! I took some suggestions like doubling sour cream, adding milk, adding Worcestershire, dill and thyme, adding peas, didn’t use zuke or tomatoes, and used cheddar. A nice change and didn’t have to use canned soup. Very tasty! Will make again!

I have made a very similar casserole from a magazine with slightly different measurements. 3 cups of rotini instead of noodles. 2/3 of a cup of light sour cream instead of 1/3 cup. 2tsp dijon mustard instead of prepared mustard. 1/2 tsp salt instead of 1/4tsp. The tomato is sliced and placed on the top layer just under the cheese. It has been a family favourite for over 13 years.

I thought this was fantastic! Much better than the boring mushroom soup versions you see all the time. We love tuna so I more than doubled it and adjusted the mayo/sour cream to keep it moist, added a splash of milk and sauteed half of a large white onion and added it before baking. I think next time I will also bake the tomatoes in the casserole. I thought the zuchini was a strange ingredient but it added some great texture.
I added 3 T of water to a half batch plus used spinach noodles

A great alternative to the cream soup version of tuna casserole! It definitely needs at least about a half cup of milk, otherwise it will be way too dry. I also added 1/4 tsp. basil and dill for extra flavor, but that is just a personal taste preference. I will use this recipe for tuna casserole from now on.
Always a hit! No changes except I use yogurt instead of sour cream, and cheddar instead of Monterray Jack, only because that is what I prefer and keep on hand. Excellent recipe!
It was awesome I used Cheddar Cheese instead of the cheese that they recommended and Italian seasoning.
Pretty easy to follow and looks good too!
It was very delicious! Thank you for sharing. 🤗

I looked all over for this recipe-it was originally on an old Great American Recipes card which i misplaced. This is my go to. Its a complete, simple but hearty meal and even the Tuna Casserole hater in the family loves it! I use 1 can tuna w/oil and 1can tuna w/water to balance some of the fat content.

I first began making this recipe decades ago when I received it from my subscription to the Great American Recipes recipe cards.  I always make it exactly as shown.  My young daughter would ask me to make it often.  It became our favorite.  I still love it.  I've never tweaked the ingredients because I like it as is.  Highly recommend.
Made per recipe, delicious! Wouldn't change a thing! Hubby and son ate it up!
I used Monterey Jack Cheese block with hot red peppers to give it alittle "kick".

I'm a an accomplished cook, many years in restaurants It was dry lacking taste. BUT! After adding 1 Cambells Cream of Chicken soup w/ half can of water. Extra 1/4 oz. sodium, 1/4 oz. pepper, & 1/4 oz Herbamare, IT WAS GREAT! Now 5 rating.
